Personally very curious if a Pi solution is working and stable as I had no luck with my NAS (just couldn't hold up to the load) and my Mac is not my favorite solution as I have to take it with me traveling and family looses Plex then.
What do you use to to transcode your plex files and are you happy with it?
My server currently runs on an A6-5400k APU. It works well enough for my purposes.
I use my PC for Plex. It all depends on your settings and how many users you have. I have 3 Roku's at my house, 2 at my moms, and sister has one all connected. I have an i7-2700K CPU.

I may be overly tired so excuse me for asking- Are the remote Roku's Plex members? If not- (again I have worked all day) how do you get them to "see" your plex server when they are not on your network? Can you Share with a non plex member?

It depends on what you mean by Plex Member. If you are talking about someone who doesn't have a Plex Account, no. If you are talking about someone who doesn't have PlexPass, then yes. There are very few things that are special to Plexpass members. The big ones are Plex Sync, Cloud Sync and at least temporarily clients for PS3/PS4/Xbox360/XboxOne.

Sharing libraries just requires they sign up.

I have plex pass which allows me to have more than one user. This allows me to filter shows for my kids and allow everyone to keep track of what they watch. Plex can be installed on the Roku and you just need to connect it in the settings to your server. Plex gives you a 4 digit pin and you just need to login to plex.tv and enter it. Or you can have them create a plex account and share your server.

A Raspberry Pi, even the new Pi 2 is far too underpowered to support transcoding. That's processor intensive, and a Pi doesn't have the processor for it. The NAS probably also isn't designed to transcode. If I recall from your thread, you are using a WD Mirror as your NAS.

If you're going to build, rule of thumb is 2000 Passmark per transcoded 1080p stream.

For example: i3-4330 has a passmark score of 5067. So, that's two transcoded 1080p streams at the same time. i5-4440 has a passmark score of 6436. So, that's three transcoded 1080p streams at the same time. i7-4770K has a passmark score of 10193. So, that's five transcoded 1080p streams at the same time.

Remember, these are transcoded streams if the receiver can accept the stream directly, and no transcoding is involved, then it doesn't really count.

I currently use my gaming rig for Plex. But this means that my gaming rig has been operating basically continuously for the last 18 months. I want to eventually replace it with an UnRaid box (Offhand, I like how it handles redundancy) but FreeNAS works as well. This kind of setup would work nicely for both Plex and for file storage.
